place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房后面 · 泥地里
place.en: Chending Temple · Behind the woodshed · in the mud

setup.zh: 胸口的木牌烫了，烫得很久很久。小银狐钻出来，看着你的伤，一句话都没说——然后「呸」地吐出了一样东西。
setup.en: The token on your chest burns, and burns a long while. The little silver fox slips out, looks at your hurts and says nothing at all — then spits something out.

recap.zh: 银月一句话都没说，吐出了她的丹炉——一只巴掌大的小铜炉。「替本王看着它。」她说完最后半句就淡了下去：「……下次……打回去……」
recap.en: Yinyue said nothing at all; she spat out her furnace — a little bronze furnace the size of a palm. "Look after it for me." Her last half-sentence as she faded: "…next time… hit back…"

zh: 一只巴掌大的小铜炉，三只脚，两只耳。
en: A bronze furnace the size of a palm, three legs, two ears.
"My furnace. Brought down from the immortal realm."
"…What's your name?" The lid does not stir.

label.en: The little beast on the lid

text.zh: 小兽闭着眼，只在你肚子咕咕叫的时候，才睁一睁。
text.en: The little beast keeps its eyes shut — it opens them only when your stomach growls.

text.zh: 笔画弯弯曲曲，像云又像火，你一个都不认得，只认得最后一个是「兜」。
text.en: The strokes curl like cloud, like flame. You can read none of them but the last: 兜.

text.zh: 炉身青里透紫，摸上去温温的，倒像刚吃饱了什么。
text.en: The body is green shot with purple and warm to the touch, as if it had just eaten its fill.

story.zh:
胸口的木牌，便在这时烫了起来。

这一回烫得很久很久，比哪一回都久。久到小满以为自己胸口要烫出一个印子来了，久到小狰都觉出不对来，从他胸口上爬下去，蹲在一旁，歪着脑袋看。然后，一只半透明的小银狐，从木牌里慢慢地钻了出来。

它比上一回又薄了些。自从那一夜替他凿完两道半的关，它便一直睡着，睡了将近一个月，一次也没醒过。这时候它蹲在他胸口上，月光从它身上透过去，他能看见它身后的月亮。

它低下头来，看着他肿成馒头的那只眼睛。

看了很久很久。

它平日嘴那么毒，说他吵，说他傻，说他是漏勺，说他喘气太大声。这时候，它却一句话也没有说。

它只是看着。那双金色的眼睛里，有什么东西，一明，一暗，一明，一暗，像木牌上那条睡着的尾巴。

然后它张开嘴，「呸」的一声，吐出一样东西来，落在他胸口上，叮当一响。

那是一只巴掌大的小铜炉，三只脚，两只耳，炉身青里透紫，刻满了火焰和云纹，炉盖上蹲着一只小兽，不知是狮子还是狗，打了个哈欠，睁开一只眼睛瞥了他一眼，又闭上了。

银月的声音很轻：「本王的丹炉。仙界带下来的。替本王看着它。」

小满问：「……它能干什么？」

她道：「它会炼丹。你们凡人炼丹，十炉炸七炉……它不炸。它炼出来的……」说到这里，她的眼皮往下耷拉了一下，「……是你吃得下的，最好的……」

小满道：「最好的什么？」

她道：「……那一颗。还有，它嘴刁……尝过的丹……」声音越来越小。

小满叫道：「银月？」

她道：「……它还会……」

她没说完。她的身子，便像灶膛里最后一缕烟似的，淡了下去，淡得只剩一个轮廓，淡得连那个轮廓也快没了。最后剩下的，只有半句很轻很轻的话，轻得像是落在他耳朵边上的一片雪：

「……下次……打回去……」

木牌，凉了。

小满捧着那只小铜炉，在泥地里坐了起来。他坐了很久。月亮从柴房的这一头，挪到了柴房的那一头。

他没有想炉子能干什么。他想的是，她睡了将近一个月，一次都没醒；她替他凿关，凿得自己薄成了一层纸；她说过，醒一次，就少一分力气。今夜她醒了。醒了，一句狠话也没说，只说了半句「下次」。

下次，打回去。

她不是叫他今天还手。她是说，今天，就这样；下次，打回去。

他把这五个字，在心里放好了。放在那本账的最上头。

放好了，他才想起来，他又没来得及说谢。

那年秋天在蒙山，她睡进木牌之前，他张了四回嘴，一回也没说出来；后来他对着木牌说了，木牌没有暖。今夜她醒了一回，吐了一只炉子给他，说了半句话，他张着嘴，问的是「它能干什么」「最好的什么」，问来问去，全是炉子。

他低头看着胸口那块凉了的木牌，心想：下回。下回她醒了，头一句，先说这个。

这个「下回」，他又等了很久。

第二天，他蹲在柴房里，面前摆着那只小铜炉，跟它说话。他说的是：「你叫什么？」

炉盖一动不动。
story.en:
Just then the token on his chest grew hot.

This time the heat lasted a long, long while — longer than ever. So long Xiaoman thought his chest would be branded, so long even Little Zheng sensed something wrong, climbed down off his chest and sat to one side, head cocked. Then, slowly, a half-transparent little silver fox came out of the token.

It was thinner again than last time. Since the night it finished chiselling the two and a half gates for him it had slept — nearly a month, not waking once. Now it crouched on his chest; moonlight went through it, and he could see the moon behind it.

It bent its head and looked at his eye, swollen up like a steamed bun.

Looked a long, long while.

For all its usual poison — he was noisy, he was stupid, he was a skimmer, he breathed too loud — at this moment it said not a word.

It only looked. In its golden eyes something went bright, dark, bright, dark, like the sleeping tail on the token.

Then it opened its mouth and — ptoo — spat something out, which landed on his chest with a clink.

It was a little bronze furnace the size of a palm, three legs and two ears, its body bluish with a purple sheen, carved all over with flames and clouds; on the lid crouched a little beast — lion or dog, who could say — which yawned, opened one eye, glanced at him, and shut it again.

Yinyue's voice was very soft: "My furnace. Brought down from the immortal realm. Keep it for me."

"…What does it do?" Xiaoman asked.

"It makes pills. You mortals make pills and seven batches in ten blow up… it doesn't. What it makes…" — here her eyelids drooped — "…is the best you can take…"

"The best what?"

"…That one. And it's fussy… a pill it's tasted…" Her voice was fading.

"Yinyue?" called Xiaoman.

"…It can also…"

She didn't finish. Her body faded like the last wisp of smoke from a stove, faded to an outline, faded till even the outline was nearly gone. All that was left was half a sentence, very, very light, like a flake of snow landing by his ear:

"…Next time… hit back…"

The token went cold.

Xiaoman sat up in the mud, holding the little bronze furnace. He sat a long time. The moon moved from one end of the woodshed to the other.

He did not think about what the furnace could do. He thought: she had slept nearly a month without waking once; chiselling gates for him had worn her thin as paper; she had said every waking cost her a measure of strength. Tonight she had woken. And woken, she had not said one harsh word — only half a sentence: "Next time."

Next time, hit back.

She was not telling him to hit back today. She was saying: today, let it be; next time, hit back.

He put those words away in his heart, at the very top of the ledger.

Only when he had put them away did he remember: once again he hadn't managed to say thank you.

That autumn on Meng Mountain, before she went to sleep in the token, he had opened his mouth four times and not got it out once; later he had said it to the token, and the token had not warmed. Tonight she had woken once, spat out a furnace for him, said half a sentence, and he had stood there asking "what does it do", "the best what" — all his questions about the furnace.

He looked down at the cooled token on his chest and thought: next time. Next time she wakes, the first thing — I say that.

That "next time" was a long while coming too.

Next day he squatted in the woodshed, the little bronze furnace in front of him, and talked to it. What he said was: "What's your name?"

The lid did not stir.

snub.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast opens one eye, glances at you, and shuts it again.

label.en: One Furnace of Heaven and Earth

exits.means: names the furnace 乾坤一炉 — the lid ignores it

snub.zh: 炉盖纹丝不动。小兽打了个大大的哈欠，连眼皮都懒得抬。
snub.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast gives a huge yawn, too lazy even to lift an eyelid.

exits.means: names the furnace 饭桶 (rice bucket) — the only name it takes; takes the furnace, keeps it

story.zh:
小满心想，这等仙界下来的宝贝，没有名号，出门在外，岂不叫人小瞧了？名号自然要起得响亮。他清了清嗓子，端端正正地坐好，郑重其事地道：「从今往后，你便叫『镇天神炉』。」

炉盖纹丝不动。

他又道：「那……『九转金丹炉』？」

仍是不动。

「『紫霄』？『太乙』？『乾坤一炉』？『八荒六合唯我独尊炉』？」

他一口气报了七八个，个个都是镇上说书先生嘴里的名号，越报越长，越报越响。它连动都懒得动一下，炉盖上那只小兽倒打了个大大的哈欠，哈欠打完，还咂了咂嘴。

小满说得口干舌燥。他从昨儿夜里到这会儿，只喝了一碗粥、吃了一个鸡蛋，这时候肚子又咕咕叫将起来，叫得跟炉盖上那小兽的哈欠一唱一和。他终于忍不住，骂了一声：「你这饭桶，倒比我还难伺候。」

话音未落，只听「咔哒」一声，炉盖轻轻一跳。

那小兽竟睁开了一只眼睛，冲他眨了一眨。

小满呆了半晌，这才明白过来：它看上的，偏偏是「饭桶」两个字。

他把那只炉子捧起来，翻来覆去地看。炉底刻着几个字，笔画弯弯曲曲，像云又像火，他一个都不认得，只认得最后一个，是个「兜」字。兜什么？兜里的兜？他想，这炉子原先的主人，大约是个穷的，穷得跟他一样，什么都往兜里揣。

他哪里知道，这个「兜」字底下，还连着一座宫，宫里住着一位老人家，天上地下，谁见了都要叫一声祖师。那是后话，也是很后很后的话了。那一天，这只炉子只有一个名字，叫饭桶。
story.en:
Xiaoman thought: a treasure come down from the immortal realm, and no name — out in the world, won't people look down on it? A name it must have, and a resounding one. He cleared his throat, sat up straight, and declared with great ceremony: "From this day on, you shall be called the Heaven-Quelling Divine Furnace."

The lid didn't budge.

"Then… the Nine-Turn Golden Elixir Furnace?"

Still nothing.

"Purple Empyrean? Supreme One? One Furnace of Heaven and Earth? Sole-Supreme-in-All-Eight-Wilds-and-Six-Directions Furnace?"

He reeled off seven or eight in one breath, every one a name out of the county storyteller's mouth, each longer and grander than the last. It couldn't even be bothered to stir; the little beast on the lid gave a great yawn instead, and smacked its lips after.

Xiaoman talked himself dry. Since last night he had had one bowl of porridge and one egg, and now his stomach set to rumbling again, rumbling in answer to the little beast's yawns. At last he could stand it no more and swore: "You rice bucket — you're harder to please than I am."

The words were hardly out when — click — the lid gave a little hop.

The little beast opened one eye and winked at him.

Xiaoman gaped a long while before he understood: the name it had fancied was, of all things, "rice bucket."

He picked up the furnace and turned it over and over. On the bottom were carved a few characters, their strokes curling like cloud or flame; he couldn't read any of them except the last, which was "兜" — pocket. Pocket what? A pocket in the sense of a pocket? He thought: the furnace's first owner must have been poor, poor like him, stuffing everything into his pocket.

How could he know that under this "兜" there was a whole palace, and in the palace lived an old gentleman whom everyone in heaven and on earth, meeting him, must call Patriarch. That is for later — much, much later. That day the furnace had only one name: Rice Bucket.

refuse.zh: 炉盖纹丝不动。炉盖上的小兽打了个哈欠。
refuse.en: The lid doesn't stir. The little beast on the lid yawns.
